description:
Location: crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/backend.rs:35-46 (FileNodeBackend::create_object) plus
crate-jmap-filenode-server/src/filenode.rs:254-446 (collision-detection pre-check).

The handler performs collision detection via
`find_sibling_by_name(...)` BEFORE calling `create_object`. The two
calls are not transactional: a concurrent client can insert a
colliding-named sibling in the gap between the two backend calls.

Per the workspace AGENTS.md "Caller identity (foundation seam)"
section, the rule is:

> Backends are canonical for permission enforcement. Handlers do
> NO permission checking. Defense-in-depth handler-side pre-checks
> are allowed but the backend MUST re-verify atomically with the
> mutation.

The same atomicity rule SHOULD apply to name-collision and cycle
checks (they are correctness invariants on the data, not just
permissions). But `create_object`'s docstring (backend.rs:35-38)
says nothing about it:

```rust
/// Create a new FileNode.
///
/// Returns `(assigned_id, created_object)` on success.  `create_id` is
/// the client-side creation id from the `/set` request.
fn create_object<O: SetObject + Send + Sync>(
    &self,
    caller: &Self::CallerCtx,
    account_id: &jmap_types::Id,
    create_id: &str,
    obj: O,
) -> ...
```

A consumer implementing `FileNodeBackend` will read the docstring,
see no mention of "MUST atomically check name collision against
parentId", and write a `create_object` that simply inserts the
node. A test against single-threaded `MemoryBackend` will pass.
Production traffic with concurrent writes will produce duplicate
sibling names — silent corruption of the FileNode invariant that
"name is unique within a parent".

The same critique applies to `update_object` (when patch touches
`parentId` and the backend must enforce cycle prevention) and to
`destroy_object` (when the backend must enforce the
"nodeHasChildren" guard atomically with the destroy).

Required fix: extend the docstrings on `create_object`,
`update_object`, and `destroy_object` to enumerate the invariants
the backend MUST re-verify atomically with the mutation:

- create_object: name uniqueness under parentId; if-blob-then-blob-exists
- update_object: cycle prevention if parentId changes; name uniqueness
  if name changes
- destroy_object: nodeHasChildren guard when called outside the
  cascade context

This is `underspecified` rather than a bug — the current code path
through MemoryBackend is correct because the same lock is held across
the read+write — but the docstring leaves the invariant unstated, so
production consumers writing their own backend impls will get it
wrong by default. P3 because the workaround (read the source) is
trivial for a careful implementor, but the trap is real.

LABELS: api-contract, underspecified
title: FileNodeBackend::create_object contract does not require atomic name-collision re-validation; handler pre-check is TOCTOU
